heard: There are more planets than stars in the night sky. We once thought our galaxy was a collection of lonely suns. Edwin Hubble proved we're one galaxy among billions in the 1920s. This barred spiral home holds up to 400 billion stars. It hides a black hole 4 million times heavier than the sun. But scientists realize the stars aren't the main event. The Milky Way actually contains at least 100 billion planets. That's an average of one world for every single star. It means there are more planets than stars in the night sky.
